question: How is Chikilli doing?
answer:
Chikilli stands out for low sanctions and approvals within the Gram Panchayats reviewed: it has the lowest sanctioned amount across all fiscal years and the lowest number of activities with technical and administrative approval in 5/6 fiscal years. The exception for both approval measures is 2023-2024, when no clear pattern appears.

Recorded planned cost totals Rs 5.51 crore across 6 fiscal years, while recorded spending totals Rs 1.39 crore over the same number of years. Planned cost is highest in 2024-2025 at 29.9% (Rs 1.64 crore), whereas spending is highest in 2021-2022 at 22.9% (Rs 31.82 lakh). Spending linked to planned activities totals Rs 1.30 crore, and the linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2% across the six years; this should be read as improved recording completeness unless the cashbook total increased alongside it.

Of 640 planned activities, 550 activities (85.9%) are recorded as “Activity Approved,” with 90 activities across the other two statuses. Chikilli also has 65 ongoing activities across 7 LSDG themes, led by Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village—with 27 activities (41.5%), followed by Theme 4—Water Sufficient Village—with 15 activities (23.1%).

question: What should I know about Kalimela?
answer:
Kalimela differs from the pattern in nearly all sampled Gram Panchayats: Theme 4—Water Sufficient Village, rather than Theme 6, has the highest untied grant planned; Theme 6 leads in 18/20 Gram Panchayats. Of Rs 6.73 crore planned under untied grants, Theme 4 accounts for 52.5% (Rs 3.53 crore) and Theme 6 for 33.8% (Rs 2.27 crore). Theme 4 represents 20.4% of the 852 activities but 52.5% of the planned amount. 

The underlying records merit reconciliation: 684 of 852 activities, or 80.3%, have no scheme recorded. Sanctions total Rs 2.08 crore, but the sanction basis covers only about one in six activities. Within recorded sanctions, Theme 4 accounts for 37.2% (Rs 77.25 lakh) and Theme 6 for 28.9% (Rs 60.08 lakh). 

Spending measured against plan is Rs -5.90 crore, indicating spending below plan across 6 fiscal years. The largest portions are recorded in 2024-2025 at 45.5% (Rs -2.68 crore) and 2023-2024 at 39.5% (Rs -2.33 crore). Separately, Rs 2.07 crore of general-component spending is heavily concentrated in WORK ONGOING activities, which account for 91.8% (Rs 1.90 crore) while representing 18.1% of the 852 activities.

(as of 2026-08-17)
